name: sfk
why: A Swiss army knife of file and text tools with some odd utilities, though it is a collection rather than a single idea.

brief.what_it_is: Swiss File Knife (sfk) is a single portable command-line executable made of many small tools for files and text. Its help lists about 200 subcommands across file system, compression, conversion, text processing, search and compare, networking, scripting, development and miscellaneous groups. Examples include directory listing and sizing, duplicate finding, zip, line-ending and encoding conversion, regex-style filtering, md5 checks, a small HTTP/FTP server, a UDP and TCP toolkit, a ping sweep and a scripting layer. Input is files, text streams or network traffic, and output is terminal text, files, or a GUI viewer for some commands. The homepage describes it as a Windows tool that also builds for Mac and Linux.
brief.why_it_exists: The author describes it as a tool that "combines many functions in a single, portable executable that belongs onto every USB stick." The aim is one tool that replaces a drawer of separate utilities, with the same behaviour across platforms.
brief.how_it_works: Each function is a subcommand, invoked as sfk followed by a name, for example sfk list or sfk filter. Many subcommands can be chained, and the scripting group (sfk batch, sfk label, sfk call, sfk loop, sfk setvar) runs multi-step jobs from script files. Help is built in: sfk help chain explains combining commands and sfk ask word1 searches all help text for a term.

brief.install_notes: No installer. Download the binary for your platform (Windows 64-bit, Windows 32-bit or XP, Linux x86-64 Ubuntu, 32-bit Intel Linux, libc5 systems like DSL, 32-bit ARM Linux such as Raspberry Pi, macOS i686 or arm), or use the zip with all binaries and source. On Windows, open CMD, cd to the download folder and type sfk. On Mac or Linux, rename the file to sfk, run chmod +x sfk, then run ./sfk. A brew formula exists under the name sfk. The Windows build targets Windows XP through 10.
brief.standout: Everything ships as one executable with no install and no runtime, so it can run from a USB stick. The collection is unusually wide, from file tools to a TCP toolkit and a phonetic-spelling command, and the built-in help search (sfk ask) makes that breadth navigable.
brief.status: Maintained, by the evidence on the homepage. The page shows current version 2.0.0.3, a release line of 2.0.0 Base/XD Revision 3 dated Apr 12 2025, and copyright 2006-2025. The homepage is not a GitHub repo, so I could not check commit history.
brief.caveats: Windows is the primary target: the syntax overview says that on Mac and Linux you must replace every ! with : and every $ with #, and escape wildcards with a backslash (\* and \?). Several networking and GUI commands (sfk view, sfk iview, sfk status for SFKTray) are Windows-oriented. Some features are only described as Plus or paid add-ons: the homepage says Swiss File Knife Plus adds https access and a system-tray tool, and the e-book is a separate 300-page PDF. The homepage asks for donations. Only the homepage was fetched, so the SourceForge download and the command reference were not checked directly. The license is BSD, per the help text.
